title: GhostAction Hackers Compromise 500+ GitHub Accounts to Steal Cloud and AI API Credentials
source_used: GBHackers News (cross-checked with The Hacker News, 9 Oct 2026)
key_facts: A GhostAction campaign has expanded to more than 500 compromised GitHub accounts and has put malicious workflows into tens of thousands of repositories since 7 Oct 2026, according to Socket's 9 Oct update.

An 8 Oct burst hit 346 repositories through the compromised maintainer accounts henrywoo and kitao, including uber/athenadriver and kitao/pyxel; Socket did not find how the first logins were obtained.
The attackers committed a 'security-audit.yml' workflow that harvests credentials, runs on any push and can be started manually.
The new variant also scans the full git history for 13 credential patterns, including AWS keys, Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter API keys, and GitHub, GitLab, Google, Slack and SendGrid credentials.
Stolen data and repository identifiers are sent by plain HTTP POST to an address the report gives as 193.32.204[.]199.
Socket confirmed successful workflow runs, with Pyxel the clearest case of publishing credentials being targeted, but saw no malicious PyPI or crates.io releases from this activity.
Defenders are advised to remove the injected workflows, review logs, revoke compromised access and rotate exposed credentials, including old ones kept in commit history.
quote_evidence: A new GhostAction campaign has expanded to more than 500 compromised GitHub accounts and has injected malicious workflows into tens of thousands of repositories since October 7, 2026.
Socket confirmed successful workflow runs in affected repositories, with Pyxel providing the clearest publishing-credential targeting example.
However, researchers had observed no malicious PyPI or crates.io releases attributable to this activity.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers' cloud and AI service keys are being harvested at scale from open-source repositories through hijacked accounts.
event_date: Campaign since 7 Oct 2026; Socket update 9 Oct 2026; GBHackers 10 Oct 2026
notes: GBHackers relays a Socket update; The Hacker News (9 Oct 2026) carries the same campaign citing StepSecurity, Socket and GitGuardian. Not in our earlier editions.
